notes:
A television taking over a room, and the three things that turned out to be wrong behind it.

THE REPORTED BUG. Turning on the TV makes Sonos switch a zone to its HDMI input unasked. Sorriva kept showing the radio station that had been interrupted — artwork, name, apparent playing state — indefinitely; relaunching gave the opposite failure, a TV glyph with no words and a music note in the mini player. One cause, two faces: the reducer had no case for external inputs, so a stale declaration and an unresolvable htastream URI fell through to the no-blank rule, which holds previous content WHILE A ZONE IS PLAYING. The zone plays forever and nothing replaces it, so a rule written to stop artwork flashing between songs guarded a station gone for hours. On a cold start there was no history to hold, hence the blank. resolveContent now treats HDMI and line-in as a content kind, ahead of the declaration because Sonos switching inputs is not something the app can veto — but guarded, so a command the user issued within the grace window still wins. Without that guard, tapping a station for a room whose TV is on flashed 'TV' over the station just chosen.

FOUND ONLY BY TESTING IN THE ROOM, and the more interesting defect: the poll cleared isHDMI whenever a zone was not playing. Which input is selected is a SOURCE fact; whether sound is coming out is an ACTIVITY fact. A TV negotiates HDMI before audio flows, so the playing state oscillates during warm-up and every poll landing on 'not playing' wiped the input — the card flickered between the TV icon and the last station for the whole warm-up. Seven reducer tests, both mechanisms mutation-validated. The reducer suite is 29 tests.

THE QUESTION THAT HAD A BETTER ANSWER THAN EXPECTED. Tom asked how the Sonos app knows the TV has stopped when ours did not. AVTransport cannot tell — TV-on and TV-off are byte-identical there, same state, same status, same available actions, same empty metadata. The discriminator is IdleState on ZoneGroupTopology, which flips on sustained silence. It needs no developer key and no second protocol, and Sorriva already parses it. An initial conclusion that this required Sonos's newer control API — and that the API in turn required a backend — was wrong twice over: the signal is in UPnP, and native OAuth uses PKCE with a custom-scheme redirect anyway. Measured ~20s from a TV going quiet to the flag flipping, against a 2s poll, so the latency is Sonos deliberately debouncing and none of it is ours.

A LARGER BUG SURFACED BY TOM'S OWN TEST. He grouped Living Room and Patio on a station, turned on the TV, and Sonos ungrouped them — which Sorriva never showed. refreshIdleStates fetches the ENTIRE household topology every 15 seconds and keeps only IdleState. Group membership is set exclusively by requestTopologyRefresh, which runs at startup and after Sorriva's OWN group commands, so any grouping change made elsewhere — Sonos app, voice, autoplay — is invisible until relaunch. Verified the payload does carry it, and that nothing downstream is missing. Logged High.

MEASURED AND LOGGED, NOT BUILT: HdmiCecAvailable in the topology identifies HDMI-capable zones before anything plays (1 on Arc Ultra, 0 on Era 100; an Amp is untested and is the case that prompted it). DeviceProperties exposes four home theatre autoplay settings, readable AND writable, including the ungroup-on-autoplay behaviour.

THE PATTERN WORTH NOTING: three defects in two days, all in the polling path, which has no test coverage at all. The 29 green reducer tests create an impression of coverage the area does not have — logged as fZonePollingTestSeam, and it has earned its place ahead of the fixes it would protect.
